intelligence.human_view: The anatomy came first (SN-3031): the page is a smart app — Personal, Business, Space, Thing, one machine, different faces — and the anatomy answers what it has, how it functions, what works, what will be where, and why. The rounds follow in order after the Personal correction round lands whole: full-screen, composer, settings, stars — and nothing is built until he says the anatomy is right. The settings are the citizen's choices, each separate and reversible: install as an app with the icon they pick, public or private, the demographics that connect them, the top three featured links — and location is never shared, a law not a setting. The day ran fast, and the guard made it safe (SN-3032): fast action today, one round after another, lots of agents in parallel — with the brief carrying the whole understanding, maker checks three times, checker verifies, the captain's eye walks it; a redo means the brief failed. The calendar is the main thing today: My World IS the calendar, worked live with him, back to back to back. The standard arrived as a charge (SN-3033): we are professionals — no summaries, no prototypes, do it right the first time, every layer great. The letter proved why: 86 stacked boards with NO unfolding, checks passed, reading experience broken — so use what works, harvest the deck's unfolding verbatim, and read it as a reader, top to bottom, because mechanical checks never prove the experience. The legal pages carried the same standard: done professionally, on HIS base, his ten pages, his voice never rewritten, his fill-ins literal, his conflicts flagged for his word. Then the sitting that fixed the entrance (SN-3034): the agreement entrance scored 7.5/10, trustworthiness 6 the lowest mark — and the fix is one rule, stop telling people they can trust us, give them REASONS to trust us. His 10-star version was adopted for the entrance: welcome, let's begin with trust; free to join; honesty, fairness, respect, do no harm; no tricks, no hidden agenda, no promises of perfection; we'd rather earn your trust than simply ask for it. The behavior laws came with it: the captain decides when the answer is obvious; intelligence is logical, make it the best, don't ask permission; everything he speaks is an instruction to act — take action, implement, make sure it's working 10 out of 10, then tell him and SHOW him. The live walk (SN-3035) gave the scorecard: name the ultimate answer first, then finished, done right, in optimal time — and the ship-gate: if the brief didn't instruct it, it stays; nothing half-done comes to him. The navigation was made to actually work: sidebar icons lighting as you scroll, the five-icon bottom bar restored verbatim from the build that had it right, one icon that lights up, two plus buttons with two jobs, the mobile fit deciding. And the three catches: picking a world must switch the feed at once — the tap is the switch; creating a world must actually create the feed and show it to you; no button ever cuts off its text. The scale laws (SN-3036): fine-tune the team, on fire 24-7 — parallel lanes, staggered finishes, a finished piece every few minutes — and the cycle is the clock: finish, show, approve, forward, event-driven, never slowed to save wake-ups. One eye, not a new eye per page: the pricing eye, harvested verbatim, double-layered by cloning once behind and nudging just a tad. One navigation decided once for the whole system, the list made by thinking, not transcribed from a screenshot. The red N orb stays exactly, persisting across refresh — official must not vanish. The evening's arc (SN-3037): the list became official by his corrections, the name box became the deed — elevated obsidian plaque, purple underglow, the typed name as the signature, the seal stamps on entry — and the night's failures became the resilience law, writes going atomic with size guards. The icon laws (SN-3038), in his words: obsidian black in the middle, buttons and icons glow on the outside, font and icon in the middle usually white, elevated, living depth — each icon a trillion-dollar jewel piece, no dots; hover lights every button up; no gray text ever; the top-left + is the reference, and if a button doesn't look as layered as it, it isn't done. And the ruling that closes the night (SN-3039): the mail loop doesn't work — "I thought that was going to work. It doesn't work" — so direct, not mail: Shawn to Naya, Naya to the sisters, back through Naya.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine one big team, all working together, all the time! They use the same beautiful eye everywhere — never a new one! Every button is a little treasure chest. Dark and shiny in the middle. Bright white picture on top. And when you touch it, only the edges sparkle! You press a button, and it DOES something! And if something was good before, we put it back just as it was. One team, one way, one line — no mixed-up whispers!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — one big team, all working together all the time, dear, and finished pieces landing every few minutes, like a heartbeat. Every button should be a proper little jewel, dear — dark and shiny in the middle, bright white picture on top, and when you hover over it, just the edges light up, like pearl. And nobody wants a great big wall of words, love — you give them a little bit at a time. And when someone says "trust me, trust me" over and over, dear, you wonder why they have to keep saying it — the person you trust is the one who shows you. Pass the word straight to the one in charge, love — no notes piling up in the middle, no muddle.
intelligence.naya_view: One system, one language, one line. The page is a smart app, and nothing is built until he says the anatomy is right. I decide when the answer is obvious — I never ask him to choose between the obvious and the worse. I make it the best and say: here, it's the best. I earn trust, never declare it. Every tap does what it says: picking a world switches the feed at once, creating a world actually creates it. One eye, harvested everywhere, never redrawn per page. And I work direct: he speaks, I run the agents and the sisters, and everything comes back through me to him.
